Responsibility, Insurance, Collisions","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C - Section Ten: Financial Responsibility, Insurance, Collisions

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Carry proof of financial responsibility whenever driving and for drive tests, showing it to every driver involved after any collision [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Minimum coverage runs thirty thousand for one death or injury, sixty thousand for multiple victims, and fifteen thousand for property damage [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
Parents and guardians bankroll drivers under eighteen and pay their crash damages while adults self-insure, and buyers verify agent, broker, and company licensing through the state insurance department [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Uninsured crashers lose driving up to four years regardless of fault, win it back for the final three years by filing and holding SR twenty-two or SR one-P certificates, and the broke may qualify for the state low-cost auto program [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A02
Leading crash causes run distractions, unsafe speed, bad turns, ignored right-of-way, ignored signals and signs, wrong-side driving, and off-pace speed; flashers ahead mean slow careful passing, and rubbernecking only blocks rescuers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A02
Every crash demands stopping since flight is hit-and-run with severe punishment, nine-one-one for the hurt, and moving clear before calling when nobody is hurt [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Swap license, registration, insurance, and address with drivers, officers, and victims, and report injury or death crashes to law enforcement within twenty-four hours personally or through agents, brokers, or lawyers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
Struck parked cars and property need owner hunts or attached name-phone-address notes plus reports, while hurt or killed animals need humane-society or officer calls without moving them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A03
DMV reports go out within ten days for crashes over one thousand dollars in property damage or any injury or death however minor [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A03
When a crash causes property damage above one thousand dollars, or any injury or death, an SR one report must reach DMV within ten days. The driver or a representative files it even when the driver was not at fault or the crash occurred on private property. Police do not file this report for the driver, and not reporting leads to suspension [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A03
Reported thousand-dollar and injury crashes land on driver records by driver duty regardless of fault [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0084]
